To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) BKV antigen‐specific immunity is a specific indicator of recovery from BKV viraemia; (2) BKV immunity is heterogeneous and the response to different BKV epitopes is highly variable, and (3) BKV immunity can be detected by measuring T cell responses to a range of BKV antigensa, but not by measuring T cell reactivity to EBV or mitogens

the T cell response to polyoma BK (BKV), measured using an interferon‐gamma‐based enzyme‐linked immunospot assay (ELISPOT), can identify patients in the recovery phase of BKV re‐activation and can predict the likelihood of recovery from BKV viraemia.

antigen‐specific T cell immune responses to BK polyoma virus antigens are a specific indicator of recovery from BKV‐associated nephropathy and that these immune responses are undetectable in patients with persistent viral reactivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological response to BK polyomaviral infection in renal transplant recipients.
the development of a rational approach to immunosuppression in the context of BKV re‐activation in kidney transplant recipients.
the immunology of the BK polyomavirus, which is a major cause for concern following renal transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BKV‐specific T cell immunity is a specific indicator of recovery from BKV‐associated nephropathy.
the BKV T cell response is a useful and reliable guide to recovery from infection, but that the response to individual antigens is heterogeneous.

the T cell response to a range of BKV antigenes can be used to identify patients with active viral replication, and that the absence of a response to any of the antigens tested is a useful indicator of the presence of persistent viral replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BKV T‐cell responses are a useful and specific indicator of recovery from BKV replication in renal transplantation, and may help guide immunosuppressive therapy.
BKV‐specific T cell immunity can be measured using ELISPOT assays and that these assays can be used to guide management of BKV reactivations in renal transplant patients.
BKV‐specific T cell immune responses are an important factor in determining the outcome of BKV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the T cell response to a range of BKV antigends is a useful and sensitive indicator of recovery from BKV viremia, and may help to inform the management of BK polyomavirus reactivation following renal transplantation.
antigen‐specific T cell assays may provide an objective measure of anti‐viral responses in transplant recipients and help to guide immunotherapy.
the T cell response to a panel of BKV proteins is a useful guide to recovery from infection.
